rows.question: How well does BERT perform on the SQuAD 2.0 dataset?

full.answer:
BERT performs as follows on the SQuAD 2.0 dataset:

*   **BERT-large (Single):** Obtains 81.9 F1 on the dev set (English) [5] and 81.8 F1 on the dev set (English, large) [6]. It also achieves 89.1 F1 on the test set (English, large) [6].
*   **BERT (General):** Obtains 81.8 F1 on the dev set (single model, English) [2] and 83.0 F1 on the test set (single model, English) [2].

Note: Results for BERT-large on SQuAD 1.1 are reported as 90.9 F1 [2, 6, 7].

no_stage_c67.answer:
SpanBERT exceeds the BERT baseline by 2.8% F1 on the SQuAD 2.0 dataset [1].

Note: The specific F1 score for the BERT baseline on SQuAD 2.0 is not explicitly stated, only the margin of improvement over it by SpanBERT [1].

llm_only.answer: BERT achieves an F1 score of approximately 81.1 on the SQuAD 2.0 dataset.

rows.question: How well does XLM-R do on MLQA for Hindi?

full.answer:
On the MLQA benchmark for Hindi, XLM-R achieves the following results:

*   **XLM-R:** 69.2 F1 and 51.6 EM [3].
*   **XLM-RBase:** 59.4 F1 and 42.9 EM [3].

These results are for the zero-shot setting where models are fine-tuned on the English SQuAD dataset and evaluated on the 7 languages of MLQA [3]. XLM-R outperforms mBERT on this task by 13% in F1 score and 11.1% in accuracy [1, 5].

no_stage_c67.answer: On the MLQA dataset, the XLM-R model achieves an F1 score of 51.6 and an EM (exact match) score of 69.2 for the Hindi (hi) language [4]. This result was obtained in a zero-shot setting where the model was fine-tuned on the English Squad dataset [4]. XLM-R outperformed both mBERT (43.8 / 29.7) and XLM-15 (48.8 / 27.3) on the Hindi portion of the MLQA benchmark [4].

rows.question: Compare MuRIL and mBERT on XNLI for Hindi.

full.answer:
MuRIL outperforms mBERT on the XNLI dataset for Hindi across multiple reported settings:

*   **XTREME (IN) Benchmark:** MuRIL achieves 74.1% accuracy, while mBERT achieves 66.8% accuracy [1].
*   **XNLI (Accuracy) Results:** MuRIL achieves 70.7% accuracy, while mBERT achieves 60.5% accuracy [2].
*   **XNLI (hi-tr) Results:** MuRIL achieves 68.2% accuracy, while mBERT achieves 39.6% accuracy [3].
*   **Indic XNLI (zero-shot):** MuRIL achieves 72.4% accuracy, while mBERT achieves 54.7% accuracy [4]. 
*   **Note:** In the Indic XNLI (zero-shot) evaluation, a second result for MuRIL is recorded as 58.9% accuracy [4].

MuRIL is noted to significantly outperform mBERT on all tasks in the XTREME benchmark [1, 5].

no_stage_c67.answer: On the XNLI dataset for the Hindi language (hi), MuRIL achieves an accuracy of 70.7% [1], while mBERT achieves 60.5% [1]. In the context of the XTREME (IN) benchmark, MuRIL achieves an XNLI accuracy of 74.1% compared to mBERT's 66.8% [2]. Additionally, for the transliterated Hindi test set (hi-tr), MuRIL achieves 68.2% accuracy, while mBERT achieves 39.6% [3]. MuRIL is noted to significantly outperform mBERT on all tasks in the cross-lingual XTREME benchmark [4].

llm_only.answer: MuRIL outperforms mBERT on the XNLI task for Hindi because it was specifically pre-trained on a large-scale multilingual corpus including high-resource Indian languages. While mBERT is a general multilingual model, MuRIL's specialized training on Indian languages provides it with better linguistic nuances and performance in the Hindi subset.

rows.question: Compare the performance of mT5-Large and XLM-R on the TyDi QA GoldP dataset for Swahili.

full.answer: On the TyDi QA GoldP dataset for Swahili, XLM-R achieves 66.1 F1 and 48.1 EM in a zero-shot setting [1]. In the same zero-shot setting, mT5-Large achieves 65.7 F1 and 45.3 EM [1]. In the "translate-train" setting (which includes English training data and translations in all target languages), mT5-Large achieves 74 F1 and 56.7 EM [1, 3]. In this same "translate-train" setting, XLM-R achieves 66.5 F1 and 47.7 EM [3].

no_stage_c67.answer:
On the TyDi QA GoldP dataset for Swahili (sw), the performance of mT5-Large and XLM-R varies by evaluation setting:

*   **Cross-lingual zero-shot transfer:** mT5-Large achieves 69.9 F1 / 52.2 EM [4], while XLM-R achieves 65.1 F1 / 45.0 EM [4].
*   **Translate-train:** mT5-Large achieves 74.0 F1 / 56.7 EM [2], while XLM-R achieves 66.1 F1 / 48.1 EM [2].
*   **In-language multitask:** mT5-Large achieves 87.4 F1 / 79.6 EM [2].

Note: The "translate-train" setting for mT5 includes English training data and machine translations in all target languages [1].
